reporting-org.narrative: Norad - Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation

description.narrative:
Background: Rapid urbanization in Ghana over the past three decades has coincided with rapid GDP growth. This has helped to create jobs, increase human capital, decrease poverty, and expand opportunities and improve living conditions for millions of Ghanaians. Yet urbanisation has been accompanied by challenges related to efficiency and inclusion, including slums, lack of basic services, underdeveloped manufacturing, and insufficient transport infrastructure. The project: The novelty of the program in a Ghanaian context is to localise the SDGs in cities. The project does so by introducing the SDG Cities global initiative to a network of 10 cities and variety of local institutions across Ghana to advance the achievement of Smart SDGs. The project was initiated by the Ghanaian Ministry of Finance, who is expected to be a key partner in the implementation. Other partners include the Ministry of Local Government, Decentralisation and Rural Development, the National Development Planning Commission, the UN Capital Development Fund, the Institute for Housing and Urban Development Studies and the United Nations Innovation Technology Accelerator for Cities. A gender transformative approach is integrated in project design and implementation. Project Key Performance Indicators will include women inclusion in data collection and strategic planning processes.
Impact: Accelerated achievement of the SDGs in cities, including enhancing urban climate resilience and promoting a green transition of cities in Ghana with the use of digital tools.
Outcome 1: Improved support structure for accelerating SDGs in cities, Outcome 2: Improved evidence-based planning, Outcome 3: Strengthened local institutions, able to effectively progress economic, social and environment dimensions of sustainable urban development through digital training resources and tools, Outcome 4: Increased, measurable SDG impacts in cities through deploying public and private sources.
